title: Alphabet checkpoint: ready for sounds
goal: Recognise, name and write A, B, M, Z.
cue: Names use capital and lowercase letters. Letter names help us spell; word sounds help us read words.
spelling: Names use capital and lowercase letters. Letter names help us spell; word sounds help us read words.
rhythm: A   B   C   D   E   I   M   N   X   Y   Z

dialogue.name: Sarah
dialogue.text: Can you spell a short name?

task: Name A, B, M and Z in a mixed order. Match their lowercase partners, then spell a short name.
story: Letters have names. We use their sounds to read words.
storyQuestion: What do we use to read words?
reviewPrompt: Recall two letters from day 11 before looking back.

articulation.label: Letter A
articulation.alt: Letter A: /eɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Letter B
sections: ball /bɔl/ · a round object for games
The letter name is /bi/. In ball, b starts with /b/: close both lips briefly, then release into the vowel. Do not add “uh” or use “bee” when blending. Hear the word in “This is a ball.”
Write B and b three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter B
articulation.alt: Letter B: /b/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /b/: Close lips briefly; release into the next vowel.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter M
sections: In map, m represents /m/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write M and m three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

Write M and m three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter M
articulation.alt: Letter M: /ɛ/ → /m/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter Z
sections: zebra /ˈzibrə/ · an animal with black and white stripes
In zebra, z represents /z/. This is a word sound, not the letter name.
Write Z and z three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

A → apple /ˈæpəl/ · a fruit
B → ball /bɔl/ · a round object for games
M → map /mæp/ · a picture showing places
Z → zebra /ˈzibrə/ · an animal with black and white stripes

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: a place where people go to learn. Heart likes her job at a school.
a group of people learning together. Is this the English class?
A thin tool used for writing or drawing. Write your name with a pencil.
Material that you write or draw on. I need some paper.
an image that shows something. The picture shows his father as a child.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.

cards.title: Your alphabet check
sections: Name these letters in a mixed order: m B t A q D y H c R f U n E v J s G x I z K p L w O.
Write the lowercase partners of B, Q, M and R. Then write their uppercase forms from memory.
Play the dictation clip. Write the capital and small form of the letter you hear, then check.
Say your name, then spell it. Ask someone to repeat the letters back.
Compare with the models. Practise any letters you mixed up.
Try again on another day without looking at the models. If you still need help, revisit the difficult letters, sounds or patterns. Clear, understandable speech matters more than copying an accent.

Cover the word bank. Say two of today’s words and show or explain their meaning. Listen again and retry one difficult word.
cards.answer: 1: M, B, T, A, Q, D, Y, H, C, R, F, U, N, E, V, J, S, G, X, I, Z, K, P, L, W, O. 2: b, q, m, r; B, Q, M, R. 3: B b. 4: Your own name; check whether a listener can repeat it correctly. Dictation answer: B b.
